question: Why can Schedule-Free AdamW train language models without a precommitted decay horizon or a separate averaged model, why is it momentum-sensitive, and can its averaging dynamics be refined for large batches?

key_findings.claim: In the tested 124M language models, a tuned Schedule-Free AdamW trajectory receives little extra validation-loss benefit from either a terminal AdamW decay or exponential weight averaging.
key_findings.evidence: Checkpoint interventions show large loss drops after decay or EWA for constant-rate AdamW but minimal drops for tuned SF-AdamW; interpolation between checkpoints is comparatively flat, which the authors interpret as staying near the floor of a river-valley landscape.

key_findings.claim: The returned x iterate is an implicit weighted average of gradient-evaluation y iterates, coupling momentum and averaging in vanilla Schedule-Free optimization.
key_findings.evidence: The reformulation writes y as a momentum-style update and algebraically expresses x as a weighted average of past y values. Empirically, y and its EWA remain closer to the inferred river under poor beta1 values even when x degrades.

key_findings.claim: Quadratic stability analysis and small full-batch experiments connect Schedule-Free dynamics to the edge of stability, but the central-flow explanation is explicitly approximate.
key_findings.evidence: Propositions 4.1–4.2 derive thresholds involving (1-beta) and preconditioned curvature; toy and CIFAR-10 experiments place sharpness near those thresholds. The appendix labels the central-flow derivation an ansatz, assumes one top eigenvalue and negligible 1/t terms, and does not establish it for stochastic AdamW pretraining.

key_findings.claim: A new coefficient C decouples the averaging window from beta1 and improves robustness in the reported momentum and 2M-token-batch sweeps.
key_findings.evidence: The refined update rescales the x-update coefficient by (1-beta1)C. Reported sweeps show gains over vanilla Schedule-Free across broad C ranges; at beta1=0.98 and a 2M-token batch, C=200 matches the final cosine-AdamW performance where vanilla SF lags.

method.core_idea: Interpret Schedule-Free optimization as implicit averaging of edge-of-stability iterates moving along a low-curvature river, then expose a coefficient that controls averaging independently of momentum.
method.mechanism: The work combines checkpoint decay/EWA interventions, parameter-space interpolation, toy and CIFAR curvature measurements, quadratic stability propositions, a central-flow approximation, and 124M-parameter language-model sweeps on SlimPajama/OpenWebText2.
assumptions: A short low-rate decay approximately removes high-curvature displacement without materially moving downstream, so its gain diagnoses distance from the river floor.
The largest preconditioned Hessian direction captures the relevant edge-of-stability behavior.
Findings at 124M parameters and 2.5–5B tokens transfer to genuinely large, continually extended pretraining.

techniques.role: Applies a short decay from saved iterates to estimate recoverable high-curvature loss.
Rewrites the three-sequence optimizer as momentum on y plus implicit averaging into x.
Introduces C in the averaging coefficient so beta1 need not set both memory effects.

evaluations.setting: 124M LLaMA-style model, SlimPajama, 0.5M-token batches, roughly 2.5B tokens
evaluations.metric: Validation perplexity/loss before and after decay or EWA
evaluations.result: Tuned SF-AdamW gains minimally from either intervention, unlike constant-rate AdamW; suboptimal beta1 restores a sizable decay gain.
evaluations.baseline: AdamW with constant rate, decay, EWA, and cosine scheduling.

evaluations.setting: Toy river objective and full-batch MLP on 5k CIFAR-10 examples
evaluations.metric: Trajectory geometry and (preconditioned) top Hessian eigenvalue
evaluations.result: y oscillates around the river and measured sharpness approaches the derived stability threshold.
evaluations.baseline: Standard edge-of-stability threshold and x-iterate behavior.

evaluations.result: Refined SF with C around 200 closes the reported gap between vanilla SF and cosine AdamW.

limitations: Author-stated: the central-flow analysis uses simplifying assumptions and the language-model experiments are small-scale.
Author-stated: momentum sensitivity and large-batch degradation motivate an additional hyperparameter rather than a parameter-free resolution.
Reviewer inference: the river diagnostic depends on interpreting decay as pure cross-river movement; it does not directly identify Hessian subspaces in the LM runs.
Reviewer inference: compute savings from avoiding an auxiliary average are not benchmarked in distributed frontier training.
failure_modes: Poor beta1 can make the reported x iterate drift away from a good y trajectory even as optimization continues.
A fixed C may cease to be appropriate when batch size, curvature, or data distribution changes during open-ended training.
Multiple sharp modes or rapidly changing adaptive preconditioners can invalidate the single-mode central-flow picture.
reusable_insights: Use terminal-decay and averaging interventions on saved checkpoints to distinguish optimization progress from oscillatory excess loss.
Optimizer state variables may play separable roles as evaluation points and returned averages; inspect them independently.
When one coefficient controls two kinds of memory, expose the coupling before adding more elaborate mechanisms.
open_questions: Does refined Schedule-Free optimization preserve its advantage at multi-billion-parameter scale and after data-mixture shifts?
Can C be estimated online from curvature or iterate statistics without a sweep?
How accurate is the proposed central flow for stochastic, coordinatewise AdamW rather than scalar/full-batch surrogates?

competitive_landscape.title: The Road Less Scheduled
competitive_landscape.difference: Defazio et al. introduce Schedule-Free optimization from online-to-batch theory; the reviewed paper supplies a river/edge-of-stability interpretation and a decoupled averaging coefficient for LM pretraining.

competitive_landscape.title: Scaling Laws and Compute-Optimal Training Beyond Fixed Training Durations
competitive_landscape.difference: Hagele et al. use reusable constant-rate trunks with cooldowns and stochastic weight averaging; Schedule-Free seeks comparable visibility without explicit cooldown branches or an additional full parameter copy.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Warmup-Stable-Decay Learning Rates: A River Valley Loss Landscape View
competitive_landscape.difference: Wen et al. develop the river-valley account for stable-then-decay schedules; this paper transfers that diagnostic to Schedule-Free trajectories and argues their returned averages already follow the floor.

competitive_landscape.title: Connections between Schedule-Free Optimizers, AdEMAMix, and Accelerated SGD Variants
competitive_landscape.difference: Morwani et al. connect momentum variants and propose Simplified-AdEMAMix, reporting strong 150M language-model results; the reviewed work focuses on implicit averaging, river tracking, and decoupling its x-update from beta1.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: Schedule-Free AdamW implicitly averages its edge-of-stability trajectory so it tracks a river without decay or extra model storage, and the new C coefficient improves momentum and large-batch robustness. Reviewer inference after comparison: the optimizer and river view are inherited, but the algebraic coupling diagnosis, checkpoint interventions, and C refinement form a coherent new contribution; evidence for frontier-scale continual pretraining remains prospective.
reviewer_notes: Read all twenty-six extracted pages, including algorithms, hyperparameters, sweeps, proofs, and the explicitly non-rigorous central-flow derivation. Quantitative results are author-reported; the scope of the geometric diagnostic and scale extrapolation are reviewer judgments. Competitor primary records were checked on 2026-08-23.
